findings.title: Accidental git submodule `sentry-repo` committed
findings.body: A git submodule entry `sentry-repo` pointing to commit `a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` (without a corresponding `.gitmodules` entry) was added to the repository root. This appears to be an accidental nested clone of the repository and will break `git submodule` operations or confuse tooling.

findings.title: `_get_event_stats` passes outer `dataset` and `request` instead of `scoped_dataset` and `query` to upsampling check
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` is called with the outer `dataset` variable and `request` (from which `_is_error_focused_query` reads `request.GET.get("query")`), instead of the function parameters `scoped_dataset` and `query`. When `get_event_stats_factory` splits a dashboard widget query (lines 362-452), it calls `_get_event_stats` with `scoped_dataset=discover` and modified queries such as `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` or `f"({query}) AND event.type:transaction"`, while the outer `dataset` is `metrics_enhanced_performance` or `metrics_performance`. Because `dataset` is not `discover` or `errors`, upsampling is never applied to split error widget queries; conversely, if `scoped_dataset` were `errors` or `discover`, checking `request.GET['query']` instead of the passed `query` would ignore query rewrites (or even upsample the `event.type:transaction` split check if the original query string contained `event.type:error`).

findings.title: Using Python's `hash()` in shared cache key causes cross-process cache misses and collisions
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` build a shared cache key using `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. In Python 3, `hash()` on tuples is salted with a random per-process `PYTHONHASHSEED` (and tuple hash mixing can also vary), and 64-bit hashes can collide. Different worker processes will compute different cache keys for the same `project_ids`, making `invalidate_upsampling_cache` unable to reliably invalidate entries written by other processes and reducing cache hit rates across workers. Use a deterministic representation (e.g., `,`.join(map(str, sorted(set(project_ids)))) or a `hashlib` digest) for the cache key.

findings.title: Substring check `"event.type:error" in query` misclassifies negated or compound queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` checks `"event.type:error" in query` on the raw query string. This matches negated filters like `!event.type:error`, `OR` expressions that include transactions (e.g. `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`), or string literals containing `event.type:error` (e.g. `message:"event.type:error"`). In those cases on the `discover` dataset, `count()` will be replaced with `upsampled_count()`, summing `sample_weight` across non-error events (where `sample_weight` is unset/0 or not applicable) and returning incorrect counts.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` sums `sample_weight` without handling `NULL` or `0` for unsampled events
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. In Snuba's errors/discover schema, events that were ingested without client error sampling (or before sampling was enabled for the project) have `sample_weight` as `NULL` or `0` rather than `1`. Summing `sample_weight` directly without coalescing/defaulting unset values to `1` (e.g. `if(greater(sample_weight, 1), sample_weight, 1)` or ` coalesce(sample_weight, 1)`) causes unsampled events in an allowlisted project to contribute `0` to the count instead of `1`.

findings.title: Transforming `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count` breaks `top_events_timeseries` and `transformAliasToInputFormat`
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `"count()"` into `"upsampled_count() as count"` (which is not valid Discover query syntax when parsed by `resolve_function` / `top_events_timeseries`, as column aliases use `AS` only in SnQL or are generated automatically from function names). In `top_events_timeseries`, `orderby` (frequently `count()` or `-count()`) is validated against `timeseries_columns` and `selected_columns`; replacing `count()` in `timeseries_columns` while leaving `orderby` as `count()` causes `top_events_timeseries` to fail validation or mismatch the orderby column. In addition, when `transform_alias_to_input_format=True`, the response keys are mapped back to the selected column string (`"upsampled_count() as count"` instead of `"count()"`), breaking callers expecting `count()`.
